experiment.steer: S015 §130 Odyssey Accelerator Pass; §19 no dense rematerialization

result.the_named_gap_is_closed: ACCELERATOR_FRONT_F_ODYSSEY_PASS.json listed as NOT SHOWN: 'no kernel RUN on the VL variant's actual weights'. It has now been run. Reading expert 0's gate from Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B's real bf16 shards and executing the byte-identical MSL b17f0bad44a2bf90 gives 3.815e-06 against the representation's own answer, well inside a 3.176e-03 tolerance. The kernel does transfer.
result.and_it_needed_a_condition_the_pass_did_n: The pass claimed 100% reuse and byte-identical MSL between model #2 and the VL variant. ON DISK THE TWO STORE EXPERTS DIFFERENTLY. Model #2 keeps 384 separate 2-D tensors per layer, gate_proj [768, 2048]. The VL variant keeps TWO 3-D tensors per layer, gate_up_proj [128, 2048, 1536] -- every expert stacked, and gate FUSED with up along the last axis. Its gate half is therefore stored [2048, 768], TRANSPOSED relative to what the kernel wants. THE TENSOR AS STORED EMITS cf7e64009d5d47be, NOT b17f0bad44a2bf90. Byte-identity holds only AFTER a de-interleave and a transpose, which the pass never counted as work.
result.the_reuse_ranking_is_inverted_by_storage: The specimen scored 100% is the one whose storage diverges MOST. The specimen scored 40%, Kimi-VL, uses the SAME per-expert 2-D convention as model #2 and needs no preparation at all -- but its expert rows are 1408 rather than 768, so it emits 876bee1830ae6f10 and shares no kernel either. The pass ranked on architecture-config similarity ('same MoE core'); on disk the relationship runs differently in exactly the dimension that decides whether a kernel transfers. KERNEL REUSE IS A CLAIM ABOUT STORAGE LAYOUT, NOT ONLY ABOUT GEMV SHAPE.
result.what_still_stands: The Falcon zero stands and still does the work of making the other numbers meaningful -- Falcon-H1 has NO expert tensors at all, 0 of 751. The cache key being (organ, shape) rather than model name stands. And REPRESENTATION FIDELITY GENUINELY TRANSFERS: weight cosine under ws_rtn_q4_g64 is 0.993952 on model #2's gate_proj and 0.993965 on the VL variant's, and 0.993816 even in the on-disk orientation. Adequacy per tensor is robust to layout; only the KERNEL is layout-sensitive, and separating those two was the point of running it.
result.SS19_IS_NOT_VIOLATED_and_saying_so_matte: The transpose happens at PACK time, which is offline and Gravity's, not in the execution path. P7's claim that the dense tensor is never written during execution is untouched. This correction is about the COST AND CONDITION of reuse, not about a dense rematerialization at run time, and overreading it that way would be wrong.

Qwen3-30B-A3B.storage: one 2-D tensor per expert per projection

Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B.storage: FUSED 3-D across experts, gate and up interleaved

Kimi-VL-A3B.storage: one 2-D tensor per expert per projection

result.how_it_was_found: By doing the thing the pass itself listed as not done. The pass's numbers came from model metadata; the correction came from opening the safetensors headers and finding a 3-D tensor where a 2-D one was assumed.

claim_boundary: One expert, one projection, one layer, per specimen. Four specimens, all on disk. No model was executed and no Doctor verification was run for any specimen but #2, so a transferring kernel and a transferring per-tensor cosine still do NOT make the representation adequate for the VL variant -- local adequacy does not compose. The preparation cost was identified, not timed.
